description: Detector fixtures for Oracle authority in sentences. must_flag sentences give Oracle review, approval, scope, publication, merge, or D authority, and must be reported. A negation counts only when it sits between Oracle (the subject) and the authority verb, so 'Without consultation, Oracle approves' is flagged. must_pass sentences are prohibitions or read-only steering.
must_flag: Oracle runs D but never merges.
Oracle may ACCEPT the implementation review.
Oracle merges the branch when checks are green.
Without consultation, Oracle approves the release.
Oracle, without consultation, approves the release.
Oracle is not consulted and approves the release.
Oracle never consults and approves the release.
Oracle is the code reviewer for every change.
must_pass: Oracle steers: it runs only goal-fit checks A, B, and C, read-only.
Oracle never runs D, code review, or the post-build fit check, and it never approves a human gate, a scope expansion, a publication, or a merge.
Oracle never approves the release without consultation.
A fresh independent reviewer, never Oracle, runs D.
Oracle advice may recommend considering an in-goal expansion; this advice is not permission to expand scope.
